name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a small Field scene object: calls the base destructor 0x00193E44 and then operator delete (0x0010F6CC). It is slot 0 of the vtable at 0x007625D8; the next two slots of that table forward to the sub-object at self+0x28 and pass the inline node name at 0x002FB444, so the class is a horse/scene node rather than a plain 'gimmick'.
evidence: Confirmed only the *shape*: 0x0010F6CC is operator delete (used by every other *DeletingDtor: Actor2D_EffectNode_DeletingDtor, Actor2D_AnimNode_DeletingDtor) and 0x00193E44 is a complete-object destructor stub (it only stores vtable 0x00758AE0 into [self] and returns; 0x00758AE0 itself starts with 0x00193E44 + its deleting dtor 0x00193E30, and the 0x007625D8 table reuses its slots 0x00193C6C/0x00193CD8, so our class derives from that base). The class is still unclear: the 0x007625D8 group also holds Field_Actor_SetPendingAction/Field_Gimmick_SetEmoteState at -0x2C..-0x10 and its slots 1-2 (0x002FB430/0x002FB450) forward to [self+0x28]->vtbl[0x84]/[0x88] with the name string 'Hors..._Net' at 0x002FB444, so 'Gimmick' is a guess. Kept maybe_.

name: Field_HorseMesh_ApplyAnimEntry
summary: Applies the animation entry currently requested in self+0x270 to the horse mesh: clamps the index to count-1 of the entry table at self+0x368, copies the 0x18-byte entry (four words, two flag bytes, one word) into self+0x36C..0x388 and commits the change through the keyed-list helper 0x005E7848(self, 1).
evidence: The owning class is now proven by the vtable, not by the body: 0x007626C8 is Field_HorseMesh_Init (0x0036671C, already confident) and 0x007626CC is this function, i.e. the slot directly after Init in the same class table (0x007626C0..0x007626DC, next slot 0x002FB5DC is its 'step to next entry' sibling). Body matches an 'apply the selected clip' helper (clamp to the record count, copy the 0x10-byte record + 0x18 prefix, re-key the list).

name: maybe_Field_ActionList_FillSlotsWithTimers
summary: Part of the routine that fills a Field action list: creates the first action entry, sets its priority to 4 through vtbl[0x38], inserts it with the priority sort helper, then allocates 0x2C-byte timer actions (0x002FB460) and installs them with Container_SlotReplace. The first slot also gets the destroy-on-failure release through the entry's vtbl[1].
evidence: No readable C: the function is exported as Thumb but the bytes at 0x002FB710 are ARM, so Ghidra produced halt_baddata. The linear disassembly shows 0x002FB710 is itself a `bl 0x002A8BFC` (Battle_ActionAnimEntry_Create) *inside* a longer ARM routine that starts before this address, so both this and 0x002FB790 are inner entry points of one 'fill the action list' routine, not clean functions. The first pass's reading of the surrounding instructions (priority 4, Mem_AllocAligned(0x2C), 0x002FB460, Container_SlotReplace 0x002A8BA4) still holds, but the split is unreliable - kept maybe_ and low confidence.

name: maybe_Field_ActionList_FillSlotsWithHorseActions
summary: Second part of the same Field action-list fill routine: for slots 0..3 it allocates 0x2C/0x2C/0x34/0x48-byte horse-action objects with their own constructors (0x0036CE64, 0x0036C54C, 0x0036CC08 variants), installs each with Container_SlotReplace and releases the new object through vtbl[1] when the replace failed.
evidence: Same damaged export as 0x002FB710 (ARM code marked Thumb -> halt_baddata); the linear disassembly shows 0x002FB790 is a `bl 0x002A8BA4` (Container_SlotReplace) inside the surrounding ARM routine, so the address is an inner entry, not a function start. The four allocation/ctor/replace repetitions described by the first pass are visible in that disassembly, but the 'horse' part rests only on the constructor names in the N_106 evidence - kept maybe_.

name: Field_CollisionObject_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a Field collision object: runs the scene-object base destructor (inner entry 0x003680CC of 0x003680B4) and then operator delete.
evidence: The vtable settles the class: 0x00762614 holds this dtor as slot 0 and 0x00762618 holds Field_CollisionObject_Init (0x003663E0, already confident) as slot 1, followed by 0x00367C54/0x00367EC8 and the Gfx_Node methods - a normal dtor-then-Init layout for the collision-object class. 0x003680CC is an inner entry of 0x003680B4 (Field scene-object dtor) and 0x0010F6CC is operator delete.

name: Ui_BaseWindow_UpdateStep
summary: Per-frame step driver of the base Ui window: advances the step clock in the core object at self+0x3574 (time += 1/30, frame++ when the animation query says it is not finished), then invokes the member-function pointer stored in the core's 19-entry, 0x18-byte-stride step table (entry = fn + ARM member-pointer adjustment, virtual bit honoured) with the object at core+0x20 as 'this'.
evidence: Class confirmed by the vtable: 0x00762810 holds this function and 0x00762818 holds Ui_BaseWindow_Close (0x003BE00C, already confident), next to Ui_Window_InitDataBinding (0x001DAABC). New reading of the dispatch: idx = [core+4] < 0x13, entry = core + idx*0x18 + 0x34, and the callee address is computed as obj + (adj>>1) with `if (adj & 1) fn = *(adj + *obj)` - that is the ARM EABI pointer-to-member-function representation, i.e. a step-handler table, not a plain jump table.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState18
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState18(UIWindow* self, const UiUpdateArgs* args)
summary: Window step handler: ticks the window widget at self+0x34D8 (input flags live at args+0x520), and when the widget reports the input was consumed it pops one pending text entry from the list at self+0x110 and asks the core state machine at self+0x3574 for step 0x12, running it if the request was accepted. Always returns 1 so the sequence continues next frame.
evidence: Now placed in context: the entry is in the window step table at 0x0072C0E4 ({fn,0} 8-byte entries) together with the already-confident Ui_Window_StartAction26 (0x002FE5BC) and Ui_ListData_BindEntries (0x002FEBB0). The 'state' really is the core step id: Ui_BaseWindow_UpdateStep (0x002FCEAC) indexes the core's table with [core+4] bounded by 0x13, and every value used here (0x12/6/0xC/0xB/0x10/0xF) is below that. core vtbl[0x14] = request step (returns accepted), vtbl[0x10] = tick. func_0010EBD8 is the pop-front of the pending list (same use in StartAction26). What each step id means is still unknown, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputToStateConfirm
summary: Window step handler for a button press: when the widget at self+0x34D8 consumed the input it asks the widget which button fired (0x0062F694); when that query returns 1 it marks the window bytes +0x134/+0x135 and requests core step 6, otherwise it requests step 0x0C.
evidence: Same family skeleton, now anchored to the window step table at 0x0072C0E4 and to Ui_BaseWindow_UpdateStep's step-id bound of 0x13 (so both 6 and 0x0C are step ids of the core at self+0x3574). func_0062F694 is the sibling query of func_0062F680 (the 'action fired' test used by all handlers of this table) and returns the fired-button kind; the +0x134/+0x135 writes are two byte flags. Which physical button variant 1 is, is not proven - the sibling handlers 0x002FE888/0x002FED34/0x002FE61C split on the same query - and which step 6/0x0C means is unknown, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction1F
summary: Window step handler: splices the entry list held at source+0x360 into the window's pending list (helper 0x00123594) and then starts window action 0x1F through the virtual slot at vtable+0x54. Same shape as Ui_Window_StartAction26/27, only the action id differs.
evidence: The first name got the virtual call wrong: (*self->vtbl[0x54])(self, id, -1) is not 'remove text entry id' - it is the same start-action slot used by the already-confident Ui_Window_StartAction26 (0x002FE5BC: 0x26), maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction27 (0x002FE7F4: 0x27) and maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction19WithCount (0x002FECF0: 0x19, count as third argument). The 0x1F/0x1E/0x22 constants are action ids, exactly like 0x26/0x27. Also 0x00123594(self, source+0xD8) is a word offset = source+0x360, the same list splice StartAction26 does with its child window.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_StepSelectListRow
summary: Per-frame step of the window's list-input state. It reads the cached input arguments at self+0x3534 (u16 button mask; 0x3536/0x3537/0x3538 are the three argument values): with flag 1 it forwards the three values to the list sub-object at self+0xAB8 (vtbl+0x3C), maps the returned row index to a list row (0x003BD8A4 bounds- and flag-checks it) and runs that row's action node; flag 0x10 sets a flag on the sequence object at self+0x3570; cancel (flag 4) requests core step 0x12; any other button press requests step 4 once the sub-object's timer is done and sets the 'finished' byte self+0x356C.
evidence: The old 'Actor_ActionSeq_RunWait' name was the wrong subsystem: this function is another entry of the window step table at 0x0072C124 (next to maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction27 at 0x0072C18C) and it drives the same core vtbl[0x14]/[0x10] step machine as the Ui_Window_InputToState* family. self+0x3534/0x3536/0x3537/0x3538 are the cached copy of the update args (same masks 0x142/4/1 that Ui_Widget_Update tests on args->f_14..f_18), and the mask/branch order is otherwise unchanged from the first pass - the individual step ids are still undecoded, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputClearList
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_InputClearList(UIWindow* self, const UiUpdateArgs* args)
summary: Window step handler that empties the row list and hides the list widget: when the cached input flag byte at self+0x3534 has bit 3 set or the widget at self+0x34D8 consumed the input, it cancels the widget interaction (0x001DAB30(id, 0)), clears the 0x2C-byte row vector (self+0x3774 = self+0x3778) and releases/hides the list sub-widget at self+0x33E4.
evidence: New: the 0x2C-stride vector at self+0x3774 is the same row vector that the class's deleting destructor 0x002FFA14 walks (self[0xDDD]..self[0xDDE], stride 0x2C), and self+0x3770 is the sub-object vtable that dtor installs (0x007600D4, whose table holds Text_MessageStack_Pop and the Item_BuildCandidateList family) - so 'row list of this window class' is now anchored, not guessed. 0x0029126C is an entry of Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub (0x00291220); the second argument 0 hides rather than releases. Step id/purpose still unproven, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction22
summary: Window step handler: splices the entry list at source+0x360 into the window's pending list (0x00123594) and starts window action 0x22 via vtable+0x54. Same body as maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction1F (0x002FE024) with action id 0x22.
evidence: Same correction as 0x002FE024: vtable+0x54 is the start-action slot proven by the confident Ui_Window_StartAction26 (0x002FE5BC) and by maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction27/19WithCount, so 0x22 is an action id, not a 'text entry to remove'. Identical body to 0x002FE024 apart from the constant.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction1E
summary: Window step handler: splices the entry list at source+0x360 into the window's pending list (0x00123594) and starts window action 0x1E via vtable+0x54. Same body as maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction1F/22 with action id 0x1E.
evidence: Same correction as 0x002FE024/0x002FE3FC: vtable+0x54 is the start-action slot used by the confident Ui_Window_StartAction26, so 0x1E is an action id. This one is 4 bytes longer than its siblings (48 vs 44) but the extra work is only the same list splice.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState6
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState6(UIWindow* self, const UiUpdateArgs* args)
summary: Minimal window step handler: ticks the widget at self+0x34D8 and, if it consumed the input, requests core step 6 and runs it. Same body as 0x002FE788 and 0x002FE948 (three copies for three window classes that share this step).
evidence: Anchored to the window step table at 0x0072C0E4 and to the core step machine (self+0x3574, ids bounded by 0x13 per Ui_BaseWindow_UpdateStep). The other two identical bodies sit at 0x0072C174 and 0x0072C194 of the same table, so 'three classes share this step' is now visible in the table itself. Meaning of step 6 unknown -> maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputHideList
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_InputHideList(UIWindow* self, const UiUpdateArgs* args)
summary: Window step handler that only hides the list widget: when the cached input byte at self+0x3534 has bit 3 set or the widget at self+0x34D8 consumed the input, it calls 0x0029126C(self+0x33E4, 0) to hide the list sub-widget and changes no state.
evidence: Same gate as maybe_Ui_Window_InputClearList (0x002FE17C) but without the row-vector clear; 0x0029126C is an entry of Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub (0x00291220). Neighbour in the same step table (0x0072C204). Purpose of hiding the list at this step is still unproven -> maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState18B
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState18B(UIWindow* self, const UiUpdateArgs* args)
summary: Window step handler identical to maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState18 (0x002FD8A8): tick the widget, pop one pending text entry, request core step 0x12. The duplicate exists because two window classes of the same table share the step.
evidence: Confirmed duplicate: same body as 0x002FD8A8 (widget tick, func_0010EBD8 pop-front, step 0x12, tick) and a separate entry in the same window step table (0x0072C1D4 vs 0x0072C1E4). No evidence distinguishes the two classes, so maybe_ stays and B suffix keeps them apart.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState6B
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState6B(UIWindow* self, const UiUpdateArgs* args)
summary: Window step handler: tick the widget at self+0x34D8 and, if the input was consumed, request core step 6. Same body as 0x002FE4C4 and 0x002FE948.
evidence: Same body as 0x002FE4C4; separate entry of the window step table at 0x0072C174 (the three identical bodies are at 0x0072C174/0x0072C184/0x0072C194). Step semantics still unknown -> maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction27
summary: Window step handler: splices the child's entry list (child+0x360) into the window, formats a slot count into the shared UI number string (count = all entries - used entries - 50, written with the UTF-16 '%d' at 0x00640025) and then starts window action 0x27 through vtable+0x54.
evidence: The 'debug counter' wording was wrong: g_007AC834 is the UI command/callback manager used by the item screens (see maybe_Ui_ItemDetail_Setup, 0x001956A8, which fills the same +0x844/+0x848 string with an item price and the UTF-16 '%u' at 0x00750025) - so this writes a displayed number, not a debug label. func_00707C1C is the wide-format entry at 0x00707C00. The start-action part is proven by the confident Ui_Window_StartAction26 (same vtable+0x54 shape). Which number is shown (entries - used - 50) is still unexplained, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputToStateToggle
summary: Window step handler: on a consumed input it asks which button fired; when that query (0x0062F694) returns 1 it requests core step 0x12, otherwise - unless the sequence object at self+0x3570 reports mode 2 in its byte +0x4A5 - it sets the window flags +0x134/+0x135 and requests step 6.
evidence: Same family/table as the other InputToState* handlers (window step table 0x0072C0E4, core step ids bounded by 0x13), and the byte it tests is reached through self+0x3570, the same sequence object used by maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction27 (which reads +0x34..+0x38 of it). The mode-2 test is real but its meaning is unknown -> maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState6C
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState6C(UIWindow* self, const UiUpdateArgs* args)
summary: Window step handler: tick the widget at self+0x34D8 and, if the input was consumed, request core step 6. Third copy of the same body (0x002FE4C4, 0x002FE788).
evidence: Same body as 0x002FE4C4/0x002FE788; entry 0x0072C194 of the window step table. Step semantics still unknown -> maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState16
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState16(UIWindow* self, const UiUpdateArgs* args)
summary: Window step handler: tick the widget at self+0x34D8 and, if the input was consumed, request core step 0x10 and run it.
evidence: Same skeleton as the other handlers of the window step table at 0x0072C0E4; 0x10 is a valid core step id (bound 0x13 verified in Ui_BaseWindow_UpdateStep, 0x002FCEAC). The name keeps the first pass's '16' but the id is really 0x10 - the honest statement is 'requests step 0x10', which is what the summary says.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState15
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_InputToState15(UIWindow* self, const UiUpdateArgs* args)
summary: Window step handler: tick the widget at self+0x34D8 and, if the input was consumed, request core step 0x0F and run it.
evidence: Same skeleton as its table neighbours; the requested id is 0x0F (the old name's '15' is decimal for the same value), below the core table bound of 0x13 proven in Ui_BaseWindow_UpdateStep. Meaning of the step unknown -> maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction19WithCount
summary: Window step handler: splices the child's entry list (child+0x360) into the window, counts the used entries of the sequence object at self+0x3570 (0x0063C8BC, counts rows whose flag byte +9 is set) and starts window action 0x19 passing that count instead of the usual -1.
evidence: The start-action call is proven by the confident Ui_Window_StartAction26 (same vtable+0x54 shape, only the id differs), and the count helper 0x0063C8BC is the same one maybe_Ui_Window_StartAction27 uses on self+0x3570+0x34, so the third argument is a number of used rows. What action 0x19 does with the count is unknown -> maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_InputCancel
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_Window_InputCancel(UIWindow* self, const UiUpdateArgs* args)
summary: Window step handler for the 'roll back' button: when the widget consumed the input and the button query 0x0062F694 returns 1 it subtracts the scroll-correction pair (0x003BDE6C + 0x003BDF58, both called on self) from the window scroll value at self+0x3768 and requests core step 0x0B; otherwise it requests step 6.
evidence: Same family/table as the other handlers; the two helpers were previously named ActorActionSeq/Payroll nonsense in the readable text, the disassembly shows both take only self and return a value that is subtracted from self+0x3768, i.e. scroll-position correction before the window closes. The step ids 0x0B/6 are real core steps (bound 0x13) but their meaning is still unknown -> maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_TextWindow_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the large (over 0x404C bytes) Ui text/list window: installs the incoming vtable, installs the text sub-object vtable 0x00762D2C at self+0x3D08, returns every pool node (list head self+0x3D18, free list self+0x3D24) through 0x0070E0B0, walks the 0x2C-byte row vector at self+0x3774, installs 0x007600D4 at self+0x3770, runs the base window destructor 0x003BE544 and frees the object with operator delete.
evidence: 'RingBuffer' described one member, not the class, so the name is now the class role. New evidence: the two vtables it installs are readable - 0x00762D2C holds Container_RingBuffer_Pop, Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNextPage, Ui_ListWindow_SetupTextRows, Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub, Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim and Ui_TextWidget_MoveCursorBy, and 0x007600D4 holds Text_MessageStack_Pop plus the Item_BuildCandidateList family. So this is the deleting destructor of the message/list window class whose rows are the 0x2C-byte vector at +0x3774 (the same vector maybe_Ui_Window_InputClearList empties). Exact class name (message vs item list window) is still inferred -> maybe_.
